newsitem.title: USA: Researchers clone virus of deadly hepatitis C.
newsitem.headline: Researchers clone virus of deadly hepatitis C.

text.p: A newly cloned version of hepatitis C virus will help researchers learn more about the disease that kills some 8,000 Americans each year, a U.S. government scientist said on Thursday.

The cloned virus will "enable scientists to better understand the factors and mechanisms that determine whether virus is cleared from the body or produces a chronic infection," Dr. Tony Fauci, director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infections Diseases (NIAID) said in a statement.

In the United States, hepatitis C is most common among people who have used intravenous drugs and is transmitted through contact with infected blood, although there have been cases of sexual transmission.

A scientific panel at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) said in March that the U.S. death toll from hepatitis C is likely to triple in the next 10 to 20 years. NIAID, part of NIH, supported the research, which was reported in this week's edition of the journal Science.
